newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks weaken for second straight day.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks weaken for second straight day.

text.p: Toronto stocks closed weaker for a second straight session on Wednesday as investors took profits after the market's recent record highs.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index fell 53.51 points to 6389.03. Canada's biggest equity market has shed more than 100 points in the past two sessions.
"The market had a good run. It needed to digest it," said Calgary, Alberta-based portfolio manager Josef Schachter.
The index soared to a lifetime high of 6401.13 points on Monday.
Trading was moderate on Wednesday as 91 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.1 billion) changed hands.

Schachter predicted Toronto would rebound if upcoming economic data showed the U.S. economy growing at a steady pace. That would reduce the need for the Federal Reserve to raise U.S. short-term interest rates, thus allowing Canadian rates to remain low.
All but two of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors lost ground, led by oils, golds, conglomerates and utilities. The two gainers were retail and transportation.
Declining issues outnumbered advances 539 to 427, with 310 stocks unchanged.
Among hot stocks, high-technology firm Newbridge Networks Corp. fell 0.40 to 57.10 on 2.2 million shares after hitting a new high earlier in the day.
The telecommunications equipment firm hit a 52-week peak of 60 after New York-based brokerage Alex. Brown upgraded the stock to a stronger buy from a buy.
Royal Bank of Canada, the country's largest bank, slipped 0.10 to 60.80 in active dealings after reporting higher second-quarter profits in line with analysts' expectations.
Norcen Energy Resources Ltd. led the downward spiral of energy issues, falling 1.50 to 33.50.
